title: Object-Oriented Programming in Java
content: Java OOP pillars: Encapsulation (private fields + getters/setters), Inheritance (`extends`), Polymorphism (method overriding + overloading), Abstraction (`abstract class` + `interface`). `class Animal { protected String name; Animal(String n){this.name=n;} void speak(){} }`. `class Dog extends Animal { @Override void speak(){ System.out.println("Woof"); } }`. Use `super()` to call parent constructor.

title: Generics in Java
content: Generic class: `class Box<T> { T value; Box(T v){value=v;} }`. Generic method: `<T> T identity(T arg) { return arg; }`. Bounded: `<T extends Number>` or `<T extends Comparable<T>>`. Wildcards: `List<?>` (unknown), `List<? extends Animal>` (read-only upper bound), `List<? super Dog>` (write lower bound). Generics are erased at runtime (type erasure).

title: Collections Framework
content: List (ordered, duplicates): `ArrayList<String> list = new ArrayList<>(); list.add("a");`. Map (key-value): `HashMap<String,Integer> map = new HashMap<>(); map.put("k",1); map.get("k");`. Set (unique): `HashSet<Integer> set = new HashSet<>();`. Iterate map: `for(Map.Entry<K,V> e : map.entrySet())`. Sort list: `Collections.sort(list)` or `list.sort(Comparator.naturalOrder())`.

title: Java Streams & Lambdas
content: Stream pipeline: source → intermediate ops → terminal op. `list.stream().filter(x -> x > 0).map(x -> x*2).collect(Collectors.toList())`. Terminal ops: `collect`, `count`, `reduce`, `findFirst`, `anyMatch`, `forEach`. Parallel: `list.parallelStream()`. Method reference: `list.stream().map(String::toUpperCase)`. `Collectors.groupingBy(Person::getDept)`.

title: Exception Handling
content: Checked exceptions must be declared or caught: `throws IOException`. Unchecked (RuntimeException) do not. Try-with-resources auto-closes: `try (BufferedReader r = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(f))) { ... }`. Multi-catch: `catch (IOException | SQLException e)`. Custom exception: `class AppException extends RuntimeException { AppException(String msg){super(msg);} }`.

title: Multithreading & Concurrency
content: Create thread: `new Thread(() -> System.out.println("hi")).start()`. Executor pool: `ExecutorService ex = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4); ex.submit(task);`. Synchronize: `synchronized(this) { ... }` or `ReentrantLock`. `volatile` ensures visibility across threads. `AtomicInteger` for lock-free counters. `CountDownLatch`, `CyclicBarrier` for coordination.

title: Interfaces & Default Methods
content: Interface defines a contract. Since Java 8, interfaces can have `default` and `static` methods. `interface Drawable { void draw(); default String describe(){ return "Drawable"; } }`. Functional interface (one abstract method): annotate `@FunctionalInterface` — used with lambdas. `Runnable`, `Callable`, `Comparator`, `Predicate<T>`, `Function<T,R>` are common functional interfaces.

title: Optional — Avoiding NullPointerException
content: `Optional<T>` wraps a value that may or may not be present. Create: `Optional.of(val)`, `Optional.ofNullable(val)`, `Optional.empty()`. Retrieve: `opt.get()` (throws if empty), `opt.orElse(default)`, `opt.orElseGet(supplier)`. Transform: `opt.map(fn)`, `opt.flatMap(fn)`. Check: `opt.isPresent()`, `opt.isEmpty()`. Use in return types — never pass `null` when you could return `Optional`.

title: Records (Java 16+)
content: Records are concise immutable data classes: `record Point(int x, int y) {}`. The compiler auto-generates constructor, `equals()`, `hashCode()`, `toString()`, and accessors (`point.x()`). Add custom methods in the body. Compact constructors validate args: `record Range(int lo, int hi) { Range { if(lo>hi) throw new IllegalArgumentException(); } }`. Cannot extend other classes but can implement interfaces.

title: JVM Memory & Garbage Collection
content: JVM memory: Heap (objects), Stack (frames/local vars per thread), Metaspace (class metadata), Code Cache. GC automatically reclaims unreachable objects. Reference types: `StrongReference` (default), `WeakReference` (GC can collect), `SoftReference` (collected under memory pressure), `PhantomReference`. Avoid memory leaks by not holding long-lived references to short-lived objects.

title: Strings & StringBuilder
content: `String` is immutable — concatenation in a loop creates N objects. Use `StringBuilder` for mutable building: `sb.append(str).append(n).toString()`. Compare content: `.equals()` not `==`. Ignore case: `.equalsIgnoreCase()`. Useful methods: `substring(start,end)`, `split(regex)`, `trim()`, `strip()` (Unicode-aware), `contains()`, `startsWith()`, `String.format("%s=%d",key,val)`. Java 13+ text blocks: `"""`.

title: Common Design Patterns in Java
content: Singleton: private constructor + static instance. Builder: fluent setters + `build()` method (avoids telescoping constructors). Factory: `ShapeFactory.create("circle")` returns correct subtype. Observer: Subject maintains a list of Observers and calls `update()` on change. Strategy: inject behaviour via a functional interface. These patterns are language-agnostic but Java idioms make them clean.

title: Comparator & Sorting
content: Implement `Comparable<T>` on a class: `int compareTo(T o)`. External sort: `Comparator.comparing(Person::getAge).thenComparing(Person::getName)`. Lambda: `list.sort((a,b) -> a.age - b.age)`. Reverse: `Comparator.reverseOrder()`. Sort array: `Arrays.sort(arr)`. Sort map by value: `map.entrySet().stream().sorted(Map.Entry.comparingByValue())`.

title: File I/O with NIO (Java 11+)
content: Modern NIO: `Path p = Path.of("file.txt")`. Read all text: `String text = Files.readString(p)`. Read lines: `List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(p)`. Write: `Files.writeString(p, content)`. Stream lines lazily: `Files.lines(p).filter(...).forEach(...)`. Create directories: `Files.createDirectories(p)`. Copy: `Files.copy(src, dst, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING)`.

title: Sealed Classes & Pattern Matching (Java 17+)
content: Sealed classes restrict which classes can extend them: `sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square, Triangle {}`. Pattern matching in switch (Java 21): `switch(shape) { case Circle c -> Math.PI*c.radius()*c.radius(); case Square s -> s.side()*s.side(); }`. Pattern matching `instanceof`: `if (obj instanceof String s && s.length() > 5)`. Enables exhaustive and safe dispatch.
